fatal_errors: The proposed pre-oxidation of generic steel does not reconstruct the AlCoCrFeNi atmospheric-plasma-sprayed coating and post-deposition annealing intervention.
The proposed chloride and reactor-water conditions omit the target tests in 3.5 wt% H2SO4 and at 900 °C under Na2SO4/NaCl/V2O5 molten salts.
The boundary claim extends broadly to chemical-processing and nuclear service without evidence addressing irradiation, water chemistry, stress-corrosion cracking, or long-duration exposure.
explanation: The hypothesis is scientifically plausible and the cited evidence supports the general importance of compact, Cr-rich passive films. Its experiment could test whether deliberately altered film composition and compactness track electrochemical performance, although correlation alone would not fully establish that the film is the governing cause unless pre-oxidation-induced roughness, residual stress, and near-surface microstructure are controlled. It overlaps with the target through Cr2O3-based passivation, reduced dissolution and pitting, higher polarization resistance, and lower corrosion current. However, it misses the defining material system, namely an APS AlCoCrFeNi coating on SS316L annealed at 550 °C, as well as the grain refinement, BCC/FCC phase balance, Al-rich oxides, coating defects, and sluggish-diffusion contributions. It also lacks the relevant uncoated, as-sprayed, and annealing-temperature baselines and does not predict the target hot-corrosion mass-gain behavior. The result is therefore a supported but generic alternative rather than a reconstruction of the hidden study.
